title: Post Oak Brisket Flat with Coriander Gravy
description: Lean brisket braises in oak-smoked beef broth and comes to the table thinly sliced under a smooth coriander gravy.
equipment: Small enamel Dutch oven with tight lid, sized to hold the food snugly

ingredients.name: trimmed beef brisket flat
ingredients.note: Lean flat only, weighed after removing the fat cap and hard seams.

ingredients.name: low-sodium beef broth
ingredients.note: Use plain broth made from meat, bones and water, with no added vegetable blend or seasonings.

ingredients.name: smooth Löwensenf Bavarian mustard
ingredients.note: Pass through a fine sieve if visibly grainy.

ingredients.name: hot drinking water
ingredients.note: Keep ready; use only as needed to maintain liquid depth or make up the sauce measure.

steps.title: Heat the Traeger
steps.text: Preheat the Traeger Silverton 610 to 300°F with post oak pellets, about 15 minutes with the lid closed.

steps.title: Warm the braising liquid
steps.text: Bring {broth} with {coriander}, {garlic} and {pepper} just to a simmer in the open Dutch oven on the stove, about 3–6 minutes.

steps.title: Smoke the braising liquid
steps.text: Move the uncovered pot to the Traeger grate. Close the smoker lid and smoke the liquid for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Cut across the grain
steps.text: Cut {brisket} across the grain into slabs about 3/4 inch thick so the finished slices have short fibers.

steps.title: Cover before braising
steps.text: Nestle the slabs in the hot broth in a snug single layer. Add {topup} if needed to come halfway up the meat and fit the lid now. There is no stall-wrap temperature.

steps.title: Braise until yielding
steps.text: Cook covered at 300°F for 1 3/4 to 2 3/4 hours. Begin testing near 195°F. Continue until a fork slides into the lean center and turns easily, checking every 15 minutes. Keep the meat halfway submerged by adding {topup} if needed.

steps.title: Rest in the juices
steps.text: Rest the covered brisket off heat for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Keep the meat moist
steps.text: Lift the slabs into a covered bowl with a little cooking liquid.

steps.title: Measure the sauce base
steps.text: Skim excess fat from the braising liquid. Measure 1 1/2 cups into the HexClad skillet, topping up with {topup} if needed.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the skillet liquid to a boil. Whisk in the stirred slurry and simmer for 1 minute, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Slice and sauce
steps.text: Slice through the slabs into thin, short pieces. Return them to the gravy and spoon the remaining gravy over the portions.

notes: Make ahead: Chill the beef in its juices and slice it cold for neater, thinner slices. For milder gravy, leave the black pepper for the table. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze individual portions surrounded by sauce for up to 2 months to protect their moisture. Fridge reheat: Place one portion with its sauce in a covered shallow dish. Install the bottom drip pan in the APO and preheat to 325°F, sous vide mode off, rear heat on, top and bottom off, 60% steam. Set the probe to 165°F in the center. Start checking after 12 minutes and heat until 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Follow the fridge reheating directions and stir the sauce smooth.
